rows.title: 2 bodies found in JetBlue plane's landing gear compartment at a Florida airport
rows.standfirst: The bodies were located in the wheel well area at Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport. It's the second time over the past month that a body has been found in the wheel well of an airplane.

rows.title: What America's top economists are saying about AI and inequality
rows.standfirst: Planet Money attended the annual meeting of American economists — and the most popular topic this year was artificial intelligence.

rows.title: McDonald's says it is revising some of its diversity practices
rows.standfirst: McDonald's says it is changing some of its inclusion standards, becoming the latest large company to announce it is rolling back some of its diversity practices.

rows.title: Why Netflix spent billions for WWE
rows.standfirst: Last night, after years on cable, WWE's flagship show, Monday Night Raw, made its debut on Netflix. It's another example of live sports programming making the move to streaming as more people abandon cable television.

rows.title: Meta taps Trump ally and UFC CEO Dana White to join its board
rows.standfirst: White's election as a Meta director two weeks before Trump takes office comes as Silicon Valley is courting the incoming administration.

rows.title: CFPB sues Berkshire Hathaway-owned mortgage lender for alleged predatory practices
rows.standfirst: The CFPB says that Vanderbilt Mortgage & Finance, owned by Berkshire Hathaway, ignored evidence that borrowers couldn't afford loans to buy manufactured homes.

rows.title: Biden makes an 11th-hour move to block coastal oil drilling
rows.standfirst: President Biden has issued an executive order blocking drilling for oil in more than 625 million acres of U.S. ocean. It's the largest such move in history, but is almost guaranteed to be challenged under the incoming Trump administration.

rows.title: U.S. Steel sues to salvage its sale to Japan's Nippon Steel
rows.standfirst: U.S. Steel and its would-be Japanese suitor filed twin lawsuits Monday to defend their $15 billion merger. President Biden issued an order on Friday to block the deal, citing national security concerns.

rows.title: Is this bitcoin's golden moment? These are 3 key things to watch for cryptos in 2025
rows.standfirst: Could 2025 be another game-changing year for bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies? Here are the three things to watch in the new year.

rows.title: The water mystery unfolding in the western U.S.
rows.standfirst: There's a rural area in Arizona with massive groundwater basins underneath the earth. Water should be plentiful there, but wells are running dry. Today on the show, what's behind the water issues in rural Arizona?

rows.title: CNN goes on trial over its report alleging 'black market' for Afghan rescues
rows.standfirst: A CNN story about a "black market" for rescuing people from Afghanistan after the Taliban takeover is at the heart of a defamation trial that opens Monday in Florida.

rows.title: A Pulitzer winner quits 'Washington Post' after a cartoon on Bezos is killed
rows.standfirst: Washington Post cartoonist Ann Telnaes resigned after an editor rejected her sketch satirizing tech chiefs, including the Post's owner and Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.

rows.title: How influencers are impacting journalism
rows.standfirst: NPR's Eric Deggans speaks to Summer Harlow of the Knight Center for Journalism in the Americas and V Spehar of UnderTheDeskNews about the role of influencers in journalism.

rows.title: 5 financial habits to leave behind for a more prosperous new year
rows.standfirst: As we say goodbye to 2024, let's also bid farewell to some less-than-ideal money habits: impulse purchases, out-of-control credit card debt and the trap of lifestyle creep.

rows.title: Net neutrality is struck, ending a long battle to regulate ISPs like public utilities
rows.standfirst: A U.S. Court of Appeals this week ruled that the FCC did not have legal authority to revive the so-called net neutrality rules that were first introduced a decade ago under the Obama Administration.

rows.title: SEC sues Elon Musk, says he didn't disclose Twitter ownership on time before purchase
rows.standfirst: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission says Musk failed to disclose his ownership of Twitter stock in a timely manner before buying the site and underpaid by $150 million for shares he bought.

rows.title: No such thing as a free toilet: Starbucks reverses open bathroom policy
rows.standfirst: The new guideline is a reversal of a 2018 open-door policy that was implemented after two Black men, who had not ordered anything, were arrested at a Philadelphia store.

rows.title: This skateboarding economist suggests we need more skateparks and less capitalism
rows.standfirst: A skateboarder presented an unusual paper at this year's big meeting of American economists.

rows.title: How climate change is reshaping home insurance in California — and the rest of the U.S.
rows.standfirst: Worsening wildfires are hiking up home insurance rates in California, the biggest market in the U.S. And as climate disasters increase across the country, other states are feeling the pressure too.

rows.title: NPR shopped for 96 items at Walmart to track how prices are really changing
rows.standfirst: NPR has tracked the prices of dozens of items at the same superstore in Georgia, including eggs, T-shirts, snacks and paper towels. Here's what got cheaper over the past year, and more expensive.

rows.title: 'The New York Times' takes OpenAI to court. ChatGPT's future could be on the line
rows.standfirst: In three consolidated suits, publishers allege that OpenAI broke copyright law by copying millions of articles without permission or payment. OpenAI counters that the fair use doctrine protects them.

rows.title: How batteries are riding the free market rodeo in Texas
rows.standfirst: If you want to build a grid-scale battery project in Texas, be prepared to ride the free-market rodeo. On our second episode of this week's battery series, we visit the state that has the second-most battery storage capacity to understand whether large-scale batteries can help prevent blackouts.

rows.title: Lawsuits allege power company involvement in LA wildfires
rows.standfirst: Lawsuits allege the Eaton Fire was sparked by a SoCal Edison transmission tower. The company says they have not had a chance to inspect the scene yet. The ATF has only just begun the federal investigation into the fire's cause.

rows.title: As immigration stories evolve, so does the language we use to talk about them
rows.standfirst: In this series , NPR takes readers behind the news and explains how we do our journalism. Tony Cavin is NPR's managing editor of standards and practices.

rows.title: California's wildfires may also be catastrophic for its insurance market
rows.standfirst: California's insurance industry was already in crisis. Now the wildfires in the Los Angeles region may upend efforts to stabilize the market.

rows.title: A TikTok ban could hit the U.S. in days. What to know — and how to prepare
rows.standfirst: Even if the controversial U.S. ban on TikTok does take effect on Jan. 19, the app won't automatically vanish from phones. Here's what would change, plus preparations and potential work-arounds.

rows.title: Party City is closing. Share your special memory with NPR
rows.standfirst: What would you say in a eulogy for Party City? Have you shopped at Party City for memorable costumes, decorations, party favors or classroom awards? NPR wants to hear.

rows.title: China's exports in December up 10.7%, beating estimates as higher U.S. tariffs loom
rows.standfirst: China has raced to fill orders ahead of President-elect Donald Trump's promised tariffs on Chinese goods. Exports have surged in the country since the pandemic.

rows.title: How batteries are already changing the grid
rows.standfirst: Renewable energy, when it comes to solar and wind power, has always had a caveat: it can only run when the wind blows or the sun shines. The idea of a battery was floated around to make renewables available 24/7. For years, it existed as an expensive, little-used technology. And then in 2021, it took off.

rows.title: Bomb threats shadowed international reporters who covered Chinese celebrity dissident
rows.standfirst: Reporters covering a Chinese dissident in Europe were accused of making bomb threats. An NPR investigation now has them wondering if it was the work of the Chinese government or someone else.

rows.title: Murdoch's News Corp offers Prince Harry settlement to resolve years-long lawsuit
rows.standfirst: Rupert Murdoch's team made the offer to resolve the hacking suits from Prince Harry and a British lawmaker as a trial was to begin. A settlement could help Washington Post CEO Will Lewis.

rows.title: Add to cart: Greenland
rows.standfirst: President Donald Trump's proposal that the United States take "ownership" of Greenland has raised a lot of eyebrows. Can the U.S. just buy itself this big territory? Is that a thing? Turns out if you look at U.S. history, it's absolutely a thing.

rows.title: Trump signs executive order to pause TikTok ban, provide immunity to tech firms
rows.standfirst: The order follows TikTok going dark for about 14 hours after the Supreme Court upheld a law prohibiting the service from operating in the U.S. unless it breaks away from its parent company in China.

rows.title: Trump seeks to end telework for federal workers
rows.standfirst: President Trump has signed an executive action ordering federal agencies to bring their workers back to the office full time. Roughly 1.1 million federal employees are telework-eligible.

rows.title: What to know about Trump cryptocurrency meme coins
rows.standfirst: The meme coins yo-yoed in value as Trump took office. Here is what you should know about the coins and cryptocurrency's future under the Trump administration.

rows.title: Trump taps 19 Fox pundits, personalities and producers for second term
rows.standfirst: President Trump has proposed 19 former Fox News hosts, journalists and commentators for senior positions in his second White House term.

rows.title: Trump has declared a 'national energy emergency.' What does that mean?
rows.standfirst: President Trump made energy a top priority on his first day in office, declaring a national emergency – which no president has ever done before. The implications aren't clear.

rows.title: News site focused on Elon Musk to launch
rows.standfirst: Musk News, a new twice-weekly news site, will focus on the billionaire and Trump advisor's influence and actions over the course of the new presidency.

rows.title: Prince Harry's case against Rupert Murdoch's British tabloids goes to trial
rows.standfirst: A trial begins Tuesday over complaints filed by Prince Harry and a senior British lawmaker against Rupert Murdoch's tabloid newspapers. The trial carries high stakes on both sides of the Atlantic.

rows.title: Local meteorologists could face layoffs amid new initiative with The Weather Channel
rows.standfirst: The new initiative will be rolled out across 27 stations and feature "additional visual storytelling capabilities," Allen Media Group says.

rows.title: TikTok is back online in the U.S., following Trump's promise to pause the ban
rows.standfirst: The president-elect said he will issue an executive order Monday to delay the ban while he brokers a sale. The app has returned on web and mobile, but is not available in Apple and Google's stores.

rows.title: Why Trump's tariff promises will be hard to keep
rows.standfirst: President-elect Donald Trump has said his tariffs will raise revenues, boost U.S. jobs, and help stop the drug trade. But some of these goals are at odds with the others.

rows.title: TikTok is offline in the U.S. after Supreme Court upholds ban
rows.standfirst: The app had more than 170 million monthly users in the U.S. The black-out is the result of a law forcing the service offline unless it sheds its ties to ByteDance, its China-based parent company.

rows.title: Trump says he'll likely give TikTok a 90-day extension
rows.standfirst: President-elect Donald Trump spoke on the possibility of delaying a ban less than 24 hours from when the social media app is expected to shut down.

rows.title: Private firefighters are helping out in LA wildfires. It raises ethical questions
rows.standfirst: Insurers are deploying private firefighters amid the Los Angeles wildfires. Are they an added bonus for all — or only for those who can afford them?

rows.title: How DeepSeek changed the market's mind
rows.standfirst: On Monday, the stock market went into a tizzy over a new AI model from Chinese company DeepSeek. It seemed to be just as powerful as many of its American competitors, but its makers claimed to have made it far more cheaply, using far less computing power than similar AI apps like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini. In one day, hundreds of billions of dollars were wiped off the valuations of companies related to AI.

rows.title: International regulators probe how DeepSeek is using data. Is the app safe to use?
rows.standfirst: The Chinese chatbot took the world by storm and rattled stock markets. But lost in all the attention was a focus on how the company is collecting and storing data.

rows.title: Costco raises pay above $30 an hour for many, as Teamsters union threatens strike
rows.standfirst: Costco is raising pay for most workers as a Friday night deadline looms on a new contract with its unionized employees.

rows.title: Businesses, shoppers brace for higher prices if tariffs on Mexico and Canada imports start Saturday
rows.standfirst: President Trump renewed his threat to impose 25% tariffs on imports from Mexico and Canada as early as this weekend. The move could raise prices on everything from gasoline to guacamole.

rows.title: Legal questions surround Trump's federal worker resignation offer
rows.standfirst: More and more questions are being raised about the legality of the Trump administration's offer to nearly all federal workers to resign now and keep their pay through Sept. 30.

rows.title: How to spend less money on your friends' weddings, birthdays and showers
rows.standfirst: If your social calendar is burning a hole in your wallet, there are steps you can take to spend less while maintaining good relationships.

rows.title: Running the numbers on deportation, interest rates and math
rows.standfirst: Why haven't American 8th graders' math scores recovered? Does Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) actually have the resources to make all the deportations Trump's promised? And what's the path for interest rates in the Trump economy? All that on Indicators of the Week.

rows.title: FDA upgrades recall of Lay's potato chips to most serious level
rows.standfirst: The problem ingredient identified was "undeclared milk," which poses a risk to those with severe sensitivities or allergies.

rows.title: Trump's FCC chief opens investigation into NPR and PBS
rows.standfirst: Brendan Carr, the new head of the Federal Communications Commission under President Trump, says the public broadcasters are being investigated for allegedly running commercials.

rows.title: The U.S. economy is still doing well as Americans continue to spend
rows.standfirst: The U.S. economy grew at an annual rate of 2.3% in the final months of 2024, largely fueled by robust consumer spending. The economy ended the year 2.5% larger than it was a year earlier.

rows.title: Trump's pulling a U-turn on EVs, but not much has changed — yet
rows.standfirst: President Trump has charted a new course for electric vehicle policy in the U.S. While the direction is clear, the details aren't.

rows.title: Trump's tariffs on Canada would be a big challenge for Americans, says ambassador
rows.standfirst: Canada accounts for about 60% of U.S. crude oil imports. If Trump's tariffs end up applying to that oil, that would likely cause gas prices to rise in the U.S., Canada's ambassador warns.

rows.title: Canada's key resource against Trump's potential trade war
rows.standfirst: Canadians have a key leverage point if President Trump makes good on his threat to impose 25% tariffs: oil. We talk to a business journalist with the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation on why oil would be the "biggest arrow in the quiver" should Canada and the U.S. descend into a trade war — but only as a last resort.

rows.title: Meta agrees to pay Trump $25 million to settle lawsuit over Facebook and Instagram suspensions
rows.standfirst: Meta agreed to pay President Trump $25 million to settle a 2021 federal lawsuit alleging First Amendment violations after his suspension from Facebook and Instagram in the wake of the Jan. 6 attack.

rows.title: Trump's pick for Commerce Secretary is Howard Lutnick. Here's what to know
rows.standfirst: The billionaire Wall Street CEO fielded questions about tariffs, China's AI progress, broadband access, allegiance to Trump and the revival of American mining and semiconductor production.

frame: Up to15 visible Business-archive cards at four fixed weekly endpoints, restricted to each block; not a full-publication census
